```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A's demand evidence points to an unmet need, not just price friction. One sourced parent quote says 'the software didn't provide the right kind of instruction.' Another describes trying 'a lot of different tools.' This suggests parents are actively searching and willing to switch. B's quotes mostly say hosting is too expensive, which points to a race to the cheapest option against free-forever tiers like RSS.com.",
    "A shows a wide, sourced willingness-to-pay range. Ello charges $14.99/mo and Mentava charges $500/mo, so there is pricing room above free Khan Academy Kids for a differentiated niche. B's sourced pricing spans free to $199/mo, but the brief offers no evidence of an underserved segment willing to pay a new entrant.",
    "Switching cost favors A for landing a first customer within 90 days. A parent can trial a new app with little friction. B's own brief flags high-friction host migration, including feed-breakage fears and loss of subscriber history. That slows conversion for anyone who already has a host.",
    "B carries ongoing operational risk that one person must absorb from day one: storage, bandwidth, CDN, and RSS feeds that must never break. A's main added burden, COPPA, is concrete and sourced. The brief suggests it can be handled with a one-time legal consult plus maintenance.",
    "Both briefs show saturated markets with free incumbents. A's brief at least names candidate wedges, such as a reading-writing-arithmetic bundle or a struggling-reader niche, that tie back to the sourced pain quotes. B's brief poses the wedge only as an open question."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence does not show demand for a new product. The three Reddit quotes are complaints that hosting is expensive. One explicitly says the user pays because the tools save time, which argues that incumbents already satisfy them. Nothing shows a segment that would switch to or pay a new entrant. B's market-growth claim rests on a single market-research report URL with no figures quoted. The 'race to the bottom' remark is attributed to an unspecified Reddit comment with no link.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs describe crowded markets with free incumbents and no proven wedge. A's own evidence has gaps. The $25-$120/hour tutoring figure cites no specific source. The organic parenting-community channel has no sourced cost or conversion data. Synthesis pricing is inconsistent across sources. The COPPA and child-trust timeline could plausibly push a first sale past 90 days. B's lighter regulatory load and sourced ad CPCs are real advantages. The pick rests mainly on A's stronger unmet-need signal and lower switching friction."
}
```
